title: Nscale’s ByteDance Deal Faces Scrutiny Under US Chip Curbs
summary: Nscale Plc’s agreement to sell artificial intelligence computing capacity to ByteDance Ltd. will come under greater regulatory scrutiny after the US moved to crack down on China’s access to American technology overseas.

title: Anthropic Makes Trading Debut With Record Breaking IPO
summary: Anthropic shares soared above their opening price after the AI company's record breaking $107.3 billion IPO, becoming the first pure-play AI lab to go public. Bloomberg's Michael Shepard said that Anthropic's leadership is trying to 'virtual signal' to investors that it takes both AI safety and spending risks seriously.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Assassin’s Creed Owner Sees 26% Drop in Holiday Quarter Bookings
summary: Ubisoft Entertainment SA forecast a 26% drop in holiday period bookings as the Assassin’s Creed maker goes up against the new Grand Theft Auto VI and what the French company called a particularly “crowded” season.

title: Anthropic Begins Trading on Nasdaq at $111.50
summary: Anthropic shares open on the Nasdaq and soar 21% above their IPO price. Evan Schlossman, vice president of investor relations at Neostellar Capital Corp., says this is an exciting day. He speaks to Bloomberg's Scarlet Fu.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Investor: IPO Is ‘Day One’ for AI Giant
summary: Ahead of Anthropic shares listing on the Nasdaq, Altimeter’s Pauline Yang discusses why the firm added to its Anthropic position in the offering, how improving compute economics transformed its investment thesis, and why she sees room for both Anthropic and OpenAI to become multi-trillion-dollar companies. She joins Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple Has a Software Problem + Nvidia’s CEO Crisis with Joanna Stern
summary:
In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is joined by technology journalist and reviewer Joanna Stern of The New Things and NBC News for a critical look at Apple’s software leadership and its struggles to compete in artificial intelligence. They discuss whether software chief Craig Federighi’s management style and Apple’s rigid development processes are holding the company back, why Siri continues to fail at basic tasks and whether Apple needs to start over with a new AI assistant. They also examine how Apple’s AI shortcomings have delayed major hardware products. Plus, their experiences with the iPhone Duo, its new face-unlock feature, Joanna’s HomeView review and whether Apple’s Johny Srouji could be a candidate to lead Nvidia following its leadership crisis.

Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord
Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic Investor Sees Opportunity Beyond IPO
summary: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, roughly 34% above their $83 IPO price, after the company completed the biggest IPO in history. Baillie Gifford’s Peter Singlehurst says the debut is just one milestone in a much longer investment story, with Anthropic’s opportunity driven both by increasingly capable models and the spread of existing AI technology deeper into enterprises. He also discusses why the firm plans to remain a long-term shareholder as Anthropic moves from the private to public markets. He joins Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Apple’s iPhone Camera and Photos Software Chief Jon McCormack Leaves Company
summary: Apple Inc.’s head of camera and photo software has left, marking a rare shake-up in the leadership behind one of the iPhone’s most important features.

title: Bitcoin Pares Gain as Anthropic Fails to Sustain Risk Appetite
summary: Bitcoin pared gains after Anthropic PBC’s market debut failed to sustain enthusiasm for the artificial-intelligence trade, weighing on most riskier assets.

title: Google Workers Urge Bosses to Give Schools Search Without AI
summary: Hundreds of Google employees are urging the tech giant to curb its aggressive approach to rolling out artificial intelligence in K-12 schools.

title: Electronics Industry Faces Global Circuit Board Shortage
summary: The worldwide economy is staring down a gaping shortage of a foundational component found in nearly every consumer product that contains electronics, according to a new advisory from the Global Electronics Association.

title: Anthropic IPO Provides Cash to Continue R&D Spending, CFO Says
summary: Anthropic PBC’s public market debut will allow the company to keep investing to stay ahead on AI, as the Claude chatbot maker devotes about 75% of its computing capacity to research and development, Anthropic Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao said Thursday.

title: AI Financing Shifts From Hyperscalers to Chips: Berro
summary: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, says record demand has absorbed a surge in hyperscaler debt, but the next test for AI financing will come from chips. “2027, it’s gonna be about the chip financing,” Berro says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: European Stocks Decline in Longest Losing Streak Since August
summary: European stocks fell for a fourth straight day, weighed down by defensive sectors, as investors awaited the start of trading in Anthropic PBC’s shares after a blockbuster initial public offering.

title: Zino: Anthropic is Most Important IPO That I've Seen
summary:
Anthropic shares are set to soar when they start trading on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab’s $107.3 billion IPO and private placement broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering.

Anthropic’s debut shifts the spotlight in the AI investment boom from companies making the tools to run the most advanced models to the model makers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars committed to infrastructure such as chips and data centers, the next test for the top AI labs is to grow revenue fast enough to outpace the industry’s ambitious spending plans.

Angelo Zino, Senior Equity Analyst, Senior Vice President at CFRA, discusses Anthropic's return on investment. He speaks with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Alibaba Sees Cloud Rebound After In-House Chips Offset US Curbs
summary: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s chief executive officer said the company’s increasing reliance on in-house technology should offset the impact of US restrictions on cutting-edge American chips, as he worked to dispel concerns about Washington’s latest curbs.

title: Nasdaq Expects Smooth Anthropic IPO, Griggs Says
summary: Nelson Griggs, president of Nasdaq, discusses how the Nasdaq has captured three of the biggest IPOs in history - SpaceX, SK Hynix and now Anthropic. He talks about the ANT listing and what to expect once shares start trading. He joins Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Anthropic’s Safety Pledges Questioned by Tech Leaders, Scientists
summary: A coalition of tech leaders and scientists have signed “The Misanthropic Statement,” an open letter questioning Anthropic’s commitment to AI safety. Rumman Chowdhury, CEO and founder at Humane Intelligence PBC, discusses the group’s concerns on “Bloomberg Surveillance.”  (Corrects spelling of guest’s name in description.) (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Ledger CTO Guillemet to Depart for New Security Venture
summary: Ledger SAS’s longtime Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet announced his departure from the crypto hardware maker, weeks after the company suffered a high-profile hardware attack.

title: US Was Warned of Telecoms Risk Years Before Salt Typhoon Hack
summary: CISA fought to block release of report laying out ‘perilous’ situation with US telecommunication networks.
